Allocation lifetime and synchronization for reservation chaining configuration tables and embedded firmware lists are not shown.

findings.text: Configuration table entries associate an identifier with a table location, with width specific records for 32 bit and 64 bit addresses and a union that provides a native pointer view alongside a mixed mode view and a descriptive record pairing identifier pointer and short name.

System tables combine a common header with vendor location and revision, console input output and error handles and interfaces, runtime and boot service references, and a count plus location for configuration tables, offered in separate 32 bit and 64 bit address forms and in a union with a native width view and a mixed mode view.

Boot memory map state records total and backing sizes with descriptor size version and key followed by a trailing descriptor array, and unaccepted memory records version unit size base and length followed by a trailing bitmap that marks acceptance granularity.

System and DXE service tables each carry a distinct fixed 64 bit signature, and table revisions encode a major value in the upper half and a minor value in the lower half with defined points spanning first generation minor levels 02 and 10 and second generation minor levels 00 10 20 and 30.

Memory map inputs record a physical base plus total size with descriptor version size and flags, while the active map adds a current virtual range and entry count and retains the same version size and flag disciplines.

Map flags reserve low bits zero one and two for late versus memblock versus slab backing, the runtime properties structure is version one with a length and supported mask, and an unusable table address is the all ones unsigned long value.

Attribute tables start with version count descriptor size and flags followed by variable length entries each introduced by a memory descriptor, signature data pairs an owner identifier with trailing bytes, signature lists carry type plus total header and entry sizes with trailing header bytes and nested entries, digests are 32 byte values, and revocation entries pair such a digest with a revocation time.
Runtime forward guard control for memory attributes is signaled by the lowest attribute flag bit being set.

Global firmware state centralizes runtime table access and versioning, physical locations for platform tables including power management firmware inventory logging confidential and unaccepted memory areas, cached service entry points for time wakeup variables capsules monotonic counting and reset, an embedded memory map, and a global flags word.

Runtime capability uses single bit weights doubling from one through eight thousand one hundred ninety two across time wakeup variable virtual mapping pointer conversion monotonic reset capsule and query operations, with aggregates for the full set and for time wakeup and variable families.
An address space counts as the firmware space only when firmware support is enabled at build time and the examined space is the dedicated firmware address space.
Identifier equality is whole object byte equality, and the printable rendering derives from the binary identifier body in standard UUID textual style into caller supplied storage.

Bounded comparison first checks known object sizes against the requested length, emitting a compile time fault when a constant length exceeds a known bound and otherwise trapping on runtime size shortfall, then delegates to the underlying byte comparison when sizes are sufficient.

In configurations without firmware support several operations have fixed inert behavior, namely virtual mode entry support table setup and embedded firmware checks have no effect, variable store sizing reports success, reserved space reports zero, availability and capsule pending report absence, and runtime disabled reports true.

Indexed descriptor lookup scales the index by the runtime descriptor size from the map base, enumeration advances by that stride while the next entry lies wholly within the mapped range, and the default enumeration always walks the global firmware map.

Global state bits give fixed positions with boot at zero, tables at two, runtime at three, map at four, width at five, paravirt at six, arch at seven, debug at eight, attributes at nine, soft reserve at ten, and boot service preservation at eleven.

Feature presence follows the matching bit in the global flags word, soft reservation further requires build time enablement plus a runtime gate, runtime capability requires every requested mask bit to be set, and reduced builds of these checks unconditionally report false with mirror discovery and reboot handling inert.

Variable persistence and access use values one two four eight sixteen thirty two and sixty four for nonvolatility boot access runtime access error containment authenticated writes time based writes and append writes, with a combined mask covering exactly those seven properties.

Device path families use fixed type numbers with hardware one ACPI two messaging three media four BIOS boot five and end markers 127 and 255, with defined subtype numbers for buses transports network and console protocols storage and file media and instance versus whole path termination.

Device path storage is packed with a shared type subtype length header and dedicated packed variants for ACPI identifiers, PCI function and device, vendor identifier plus trailing data, relative offset ranges, memory mapped ranges, and file names, unified by a packed union exposing the header and selected member views.

Firmware to native range translation widens the start downward and the end upward to page boundaries and recomputes length as the count of pages spanned, using downward rounding for the base and upward rounding for the end.

Variable handling separates operations from state, with operations bundling read enumerate write and query entry points including nonblocking write and query forms, and state pairing a kernel object set with a reference to the active operations.

Secure boot reporting has four states for unset unknown disabled and enabled, where absence of boot state selects disabled, failure to read selects unknown, and otherwise a cleared boot indicator or active setup mode selects disabled with enabled reserved for the remaining case.

Virtual firmware invocation is surrounded by architecture setup and teardown, preserves a flags word across the target call, routes through an architecture dispatch hook, and verifies preservation of that flags word after return.

Seed and log carriers use counted trailing storage, namely a seed length with trailing entropy and a fixed seed size, a TPM log with total and preboot sizes version and trailing bytes, and a final events table with version count and trailing events.

Runtime work identifiers enumerate a none value plus time wakeup variable query monotonic reset capsule and platform handler operations, and queued work carries an argument block status completion signal identifier caller identity and an embedded schedulable work item.

Reservation and table carriers share a header plus trailing array pattern, with reservation tracking allocated size used count chained next address and base size pairs, MOK entries pairing a fixed length name with size and trailing bytes in packed form, secret and initial ramdisk areas recording base and size, and embedded firmware linking name data and length into a list.

Fixed sizing and mode facts state a 32 byte seed, a 1024 character variable name limit, an 8 byte embedded firmware prefix, read only zero versus read write one variable operation modes, reservation count as total minus header divided by one entry size, variable GUID text length aliasing UUID string length, and fixed GUIDs for acceptance logging and secret header tables.
Configuration table usability defaults to always usable and only in hypervisor aware builds is the decision delegated to a hypervisor check keyed by table identity and address.
MOK variable table management in this build is inert, with initialization having no effect and iteration and name lookup always indicating absence.

Two callback roles are defined, one adjusting memory attribute permissions for a descriptor within a given address space with a flag controlling the direction, and one receiving a source name during element enumeration.
The embedded firmware header carries a single inclusion guard that ensures its declarations are processed at most once per translation unit.
Flag testing depends on an external bit operation owned by another dossier.
